In this tutorial, we try to create a table that is close to ([Table 1](https://www.nejm.org/cms/10.1056/NEJMoa062249/asset/c676621f-111e-4299-a7a3-082bbe922f9a/assets/images/large/nejmoa062249_t1.jpg){target="_blank"} from the journal [Treatment of Periodontal Disease and the Risk of Preterm Birth](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa062249){target="_blank"}.

We start first by choosing the relevant columns to make Table 1.

```{webr}
#| label: load opt data for table 1
#| envir: table_1
#| autorun: true
opt_data <- readRDS("data/opt_data.rds") |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education",
      "Prev.preg","Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth",
      "Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab", 
      "Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc")
  )
```

As the final output looks complex, let's break the task down to simpler tasks.

## Building Age, Race and Education Summary Table

This task involves creating a summary table for age, race and number of years of education stratified by treatment group.

Here is the dataset required.

```{webr}
#| label: load opt data for age summary table
#| envir: table_1
#| autorun: true
opt_age_race_data <- opt_data |> 
  dplyr::select(
    c("PID", "Group", 
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education")
  )

opt_age_race_data |> 
  reactable::reactable(
    filterable = TRUE,
    paginationType = "jump",
    defaultPageSize = 5,
    minRows = 5)
```

Let's try to build a summary table from `opt_age_race_data` using the default parameters of [`gtsummary::tbl_summary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_summary.html){target="_blank"}. We can see that table is giving a descriptive statistics of the overall population. It even display the statistics the patient ID.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table
#| label: age race and education basic table default parameters
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary()

opt_age_race_table
```

### `include` and `by` parameter

To exclude the patient ID being displayed, we set the parameter `include` a vector of column names to include in the summary table. To stratify the table by treatment group, we set the parameter `by = "Group"`.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table
#| label: age race and education basic table with include and by
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

### `type` parameter

Observe that the (continuous) variable `Age` is expressed as Median (Q1, Q3) while categorical variables are expressed as n (%). Variables with two categories (dichotomous) like `White` and `Hisp` are displayed differently to those with multiple categories like `Education`.

We can use the function [`gtsummary::assign_summary_type`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/assign_summary_type.html){target="_blank"} to identify the default summary type for each variable

```{webr}
#| caption: view summary type
#| label: find default summary type
#| envir: table_1
summary_type <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::assign_summary_type(
    variables = c("Group" ,"Age", "White", 
                  "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    value =  NULL
  )

summary_type
```

On the other hand, the `type` parameter in the [`gtsummary::tbl_summary`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_summary.html){target="_blank"} allows us to specify the summary type for each variable. The `type` parameter accepts a [list of formulas](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/syntax.html#formula-and-list-selectors){target="_blank"} as input.

Below is an example which we change the variable `White` and `Black` from dichotomous to categorical.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic assign type
#| label: age race and education basic table assign with type
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    type = list(
      c("White", "Black") ~ "categorical"
    ),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

### `statistics` parameter

Next, we need to ensure that 
-  age is expressed in "means±SD". 
-  race and education is expressed in "no. (%)" (already done in default mode).

This can be achieved by using the `statistic` parameter which help users specify the statistics presented in the table. Like the `type` parameter, it accepts a [list of formulas](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/syntax.html#formula-and-list-selectors){target="_blank"} as input.

Below are some examples on how it can be done.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 
Click on the different tabs.

### Variable Names

We can list each variable individually as a character vector.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table statistics list all variables
#| label: age race and education basic table attempt present statistics by variable name
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c(
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education",
    ),
    statistic = list(
      c("Age") ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      c("White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education") ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

### Use Helpers

We can use `all_` helper functions like [`gtsummary::all_continuous()`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/select_helpers.html){target="_blank"}  and [`gtsummary::all_categorical()`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/select_helpers.html){target="_blank"} to make the code concise.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table statistics list all variables
#| label: age race and education basic table attempt present statistics by helper function
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c(
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education",
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

:::

It can be observed that the displayed values `{mean}±{sd}` and `{n} ({p})` are interpreted using [glue::glue()](https://glue.tidyverse.org/reference/glue.html){target="_blank"} syntax: a name that appears between curly brackets will be interpreted as a function name and the formatted result of that function will be placed in the table.

In `gtsummary`, some precalculated statistics availiable for display are

For categorical/dichotomous variable:

-  {n} for frequency.
-  {N} for denominator.
-  {p} for percent.

For continuous variable:

-  {median} for median. 
-  {mean} for mean. 
-  {sd} for standard deviation. 
-  {min} for minimum.
-  {max} for maximum.
-  {p##} for percentile where ## is an integer from 0 to 100.\n For example, {p25} is the 25th percentile calculating using `p25: quantile(probs=0.25, type=2)`.

A full list is provided [here](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/tbl_summary.html#statistic-argument){target="_blank"}.

Feel free to experiment with the different statistics below.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 
Click on the different tabs.

### Single Line

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table different stats
#| label: age race and education basic table attempt different stats single line
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{median} ({p25}, {p75})",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n}/{N} ({p}%)"
    ),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

### Multiple Line

Sometimes, there may be a need to display continuous variables statistical summaries in multiple lines. To do that, you can change the variable `type` from `continuous` to `continuous2`.

```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education basic table different stats
#| label: age race and education basic table attempt different stats multiple line
#| envir: table_1
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education"),
    type = list("Age" ~ "continuous2"),
    statistic = list(
      "Age" ~ c(
        "{mean}±{sd}",
        "{median} ({p25}, {p75})"
      ),
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n}/{N} ({p}%)"
    ),
    by = "Group",    
  )

opt_age_race_table
```

:::

### Formatting in `gtsummary`

If we take a look at ([Table 1](https://www.nejm.org/cms/10.1056/NEJMoa062249/asset/c676621f-111e-4299-a7a3-082bbe922f9a/assets/images/large/nejmoa062249_t1.jpg){target="_blank"} from the journal [Treatment of Periodontal Disease and the Risk of Preterm Birth](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa062249){target="_blank"}, the mean, standard deviation (sd) and percentage are expressed in 1 decimal place.

In `gtsummary`, we can specify the numerical format to display a given statistical result using the `digits` parameter. Though it accepts a [list of formulas](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/syntax.html#formula-and-list-selectors){target="_blank"} as input, it is also restricted based on what input is given to the `statistic` parameter. 

Before we get to the `digits` parameter, let's take a look at some default formatting from `gtsummary`

::: {.panel-tabset}

### 
Click on the different tabs.

### style_number()

[`gtsummary::style_number`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/style_number.html){target="_blank"} is the default style that `gtsummary` used internally to style the number.

```{webr}
#| caption: style number in gtsummary
#| label: style number in gtsummary simple
#| envir: table_1
c(0.111, 12.3) |> gtsummary::style_number(digits = 2)
```

It has many flexible parameter to use and explore.

```{webr}
#| caption: style number in gtsummary
#| label: style number in gtsummary advanced
#| envir: table_1
c(1110, 1200000.36, NA, 0.25) |> 
  gtsummary::style_number(
    digits = c(2, 0, 0, 5),
    big.mark = ",",
    decimal.mark = ".",
    scale = 0.001,
    prefix = "$",
    suffix = "K",
    na = "Not Applicable",
  )

```

### style_percent()

[`gtsummary::style_percent`](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/gtsummary/reference/style_percent.html){target="_blank"} is the default style that `gtsummary` used internally to style percentages in proportions of categorical variables.

Observe that 

- All values are multiplied by 100.
- Negative values are set to `NA`.
- Positive numbers less than 0.1% are represented as `<0.1`.   
- Numbers less than 10% (exclusive) are rounded to `digits + 1` places.

```{webr}
#| caption: style percent in gtsummary
#| label: style percent in gtsummary simple
#| envir: table_1
percent_vals <- c(
  -1, 0, 
  0.0001, 0.0005,
  0.001 , 0.005, 
  0.01, 0.05,
  0.10, 0.445, 0.99, 1, 1.45
)
  
percent_vals |> 
  gtsummary::style_percent(digits = 0)
```

## Just the code


```{webr}
#| caption: age race and education summary table
#| label: age race and education summary table
#| envir: table_1
# add_p() needs R package broom
opt_age_race_table <- opt_age_race_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c(
      "Age", "White", "Black", "Hisp", "Education",
    ),
    by = "Group",
    missing = "no",
    label = list(
      "Age" ~ "Age - yr",
      "White" ~ "White",
      "Black" ~ "Black",
      "Hisp" ~ "Hispanic",
      "Education" ~ "Education - no. (%)"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)",
    variables = c("White", "Black", "Hisp")
  )|> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_age_race_table
```

```{webr}
#| caption: age previous preg summary table
#| label: age previous preg summary table
#| envir: table_1
# add_p() needs R package broom
opt_previous_preg_data <- opt_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c(
      "Prev.preg","Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth",
      "Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab"
    ),
    by = "Group",
    missing = "no",
    label = list(
      "Prev.preg" ~ "Any pregancy",
      "Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab" ~ "Any live preterm birth, abortion, or stillbirth",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth" ~ "Live preterm birth",
      "Spont.ab" ~ "Spontaneous abortion",
      "Induced.ab" ~ "Induced abortion",
      "Any.stillbirth" ~ "Stillbirth"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Previous pregnancies - no. (%)",
    variables = c(
      "Prev.preg","Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab",
      "previous_live_preterm_birth",
      "Spont.ab", "Induced.ab", "Any.stillbirth",
      "Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab"
    )
  )|> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_previous_preg_data
```

```{webr}
#| caption: clinical summary table
#| label: clinical summary table
#| envir: table_1
p_value_style <- function(x) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    x == 1 ~ "1.0",
    x > 0.99 & x < 1 ~ "0.99",
    .default = gtsummary::style_pvalue(x, digits = 2)
  )
}
opt_clincal_data <- opt_data |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    include = c("Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc"),
    by = "Group",
    missing = "no",
    label = list(
      "Diabetes" ~ "Diabetes",
      "Hypertension" ~ "Chronic hypertension",
      "Use.Alc" ~ "Self-reported alcohol use"
    ),
    statistic = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}±{sd}",
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p})"
    ),
    digits = list(
      gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ 1,
      gtsummary::all_categorical() ~ c(0, 1)
    )
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_variable_group_header(
    header = "Coexisiting medical condition - no. (%)",
    variables = c("Diabetes", "Hypertension", "Use.Alc")
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::add_p(
    pvalue_fun = p_value_style
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header()

opt_clincal_data
```

```{webr}
#| caption: stack table1
#| label: stack table1
#| envir: table_1
# See table1$table_body
# *, †, ‡, §, ‖, ¶, **, ††
# table1 |> gtsummary::show_header_names()
# gtsummary::modify_footnote_symbol need at least 2 symbols
table1 <- gtsummary::tbl_stack(
    list(opt_age_race_table, opt_previous_preg_data, opt_clincal_data)
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_header(
    stat_1 = "**Control Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    stat_2 = "**Treatment Group**  \n**(N = {n})**",
    p.value = "**P value**",
    text_interpret = "md"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::remove_footnote_header() |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Race or ethnic group was reported by the patients. Some women selected more than one category and were included in all.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["label"]] == "Race or ethnic group - no. (%)" & .data[["row_type"]] == "variable_group"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Some patients reported more than one event.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["label"]] %in% c("Previous pregnancies - no. (%)")  & .data[["row_type"]] == "variable_group"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Percentages are based on 263 women in the control group and 261 women in the treatment group who had had any live births.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["var_label"]] %in% c("Live preterm birth")  & .data[["row_type"]] == "label"
  ) |> 
  gtsummary::modify_footnote_body(
    footnote = "Percentages are based on 305 women in the control group and 306 women in the treatment group who had had any previous pregnacies.",
    columns = "label",
    rows = .data[["var_label"]] %in% c("Spontaneous abortion", "Induced abortion", "Stillbirth")  & .data[["row_type"]] == "label"
  ) |> 
  # gtsummary::modify_footnote_symbol(
  #   symbol = c("†")
  # ) |> 
  gtsummary::as_gt() |> 
  gt::tab_header(
    title = "Table 1. Baseline Characteristics of the Study Patients"
  ) |> 
  gt::tab_options(heading.align = "left") |> 
  gt::tab_footnote(
    footnote = "Plus-minus values are means±SD.",
    locations = gt::cells_title(groups = "title")
  ) |> 
  gt::opt_footnote_marks(marks = c("*", "†", "‡", "§", "¶")) |> 
  gt::opt_footnote_spec(
    spec_ref = "i",   # Removes '^' (superscript), keeps italics 'i'
    spec_ftr = "x"    # Unstyled or baseline text for the footer
  )

table1
```
